ai.title: Add build scripts to backend and scripts packages
ai.summary: Added `build` script to `backend/package.json` running `tsc` and `tsc-alias`. Updated root `package.json` workspaces to include `scripts`. Renamed `scripts/package.json` name to `codebuff-scripts` and updated its `typecheck` script to depend on `common` and `backend` builds. This ensures typechecking in the scripts package validates against compiled backend types.

eli5.text: The engineering team added the ability for their helper tools to compile TypeScript code into a format ready for use, similar to how a document processor checks formatting before publishing. When developers run checks on the tools package, it now automatically compiles dependencies from other parts of the system first, ensuring type validation works correctly. You wouldn't notice any difference in the assistant's responses or features - this purely helps developers catch errors in the helper tools before they affect anything you use.

ai.title: Fix prompt overflow via Anthropic token fudge factor
ai.summary: Token counting now applies a 1.35x multiplier to Anthropic models to prevent prompt overflow, as Anthropic encodes tokens less efficiently than GPT-4o. System prompt budgeting reduced misc tokens from 20k to 10k and quantized file tree budgets to 30k increments to preserve caching. Empty directories are skipped in file tree generation, and 'go' added to skipped terminal commands. Changes in backend/src/util/token-counter.ts, backend/src/system-prompt.ts, common/src/constants.ts, common/src/util/file.ts.

eli5.text: When you write a long message to an Anthropic-powered assistant, your words sometimes get counted as using more of the assistant's attention than they actually do, which can cause it to run out of room before you're finished. The system now adds a safety buffer when measuring this, so longer conversations are less likely to get cut off, and it focuses that saved room on showing you your project files. As a result, you'll notice your project's file structure appears more reliably in your prompts without the assistant losing track mid-request.

ai.title: Remove debug logging in getSearchSystemPrompt
ai.summary: Deleted stray `console.log` call in `getSearchSystemPrompt` within `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Prevents unnecessary stdout noise during search prompt generation. Scope limited to backend system prompt logic.

eli5.text: A stray debug print statement that was accidentally left in the backend code has been removed. This was a small behind-the-scenes cleanup that prevents unnecessary log noise when generating search prompts. The change is live today and has no visible effect on functionality for users.

ai.title: System prompt symbol pruning uses min heap
ai.summary: System prompt generation now prunes symbols by score using a new `MinHeap` utility in `common/src/util/min-heap.ts`. This replaces previous file-based sorting logic in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` with an O(n log k) approach for better performance. The change affects core prompt assembly logic, removing lodash `sortBy` dependency in favor of custom heap operations.

eli5.text: The assistant now picks the most useful parts of your project files faster by keeping only the top-ranked sections and dropping the rest, instead of sorting through an entire list every time. This happens behind the scenes during prompt assembly and you would not see a visual change, but the assistant should be able to prepare its response a bit quicker when working with large codebases. The improvement is live today.

ai.title: Condense web knowledge documentation
ai.summary: Rewrote web/knowledge.md to remove verbose UI pattern descriptions, component architecture details, and security considerations. Reduced file size from 1159 to 172 lines by stripping redundant guidance on terminal components, plan types, and code snippets. Scope limited to documentation file. No code logic or API behavior changed.

eli5.text: If you opened Codebuff's web instructions document today, you'd find it's been heavily condensed, what used to be a long guide packed with detailed steps about colors, screen effects, and technical layout rules has been rewritten into a short, bare-bones reference. This was purely a behind-the-scenes cleanup of internal documentation, so nothing on the actual website or app works differently now, but anyone who previously relied on those detailed setup notes will find the file much shorter and less instructive.

ai.title: Delete obsolete knowledge docs
ai.summary: Removed `modes.knowledge.md`, `musings.knowledge.md`, and `todo.knowledge.md` from repository root. Files contained outdated implementation plans and scratch notes for legacy Codebuff/Manicode features. Pure documentation cleanup; no runtime code or config changes.

eli5.text: The project deleted three old note files that contained outdated plans and scratch work from previous features no longer in use. These files lived at the top level of the project and held written-down reminders about how certain settings should work and what still needed building, but they had not been updated and no longer matched the current system. If you happened to browse the project root, you would notice these three text files are gone, but nothing else around them changed and nothing stopped working as a result.

ai.title: Fixed file tree budget in agent prompt
ai.summary: Agent system prompt enforces fixed token budgets for files (100k/25k lite) and file tree (20k/5k lite), removing dynamic calculation and conditional exclusion. Search prompt increments adjusted from 30k to 20k. Scope: backend/src/main-prompt.ts, backend/src/system-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now uses fixed space limits for reading your project files and folder listings instead of calculating them each time. File allowances stayed at 25,000 tokens for lighter tasks and rose from 80,000 to 100,000 for full tasks, while folder listings are clamped to 20,000 tokens (5,000 for lighter tasks). Search snippets get slightly smaller slices, reduced from 30,000 to 20,000 token blocks, so the assistant can keep more room for your actual conversation.

ai.title: Tiered file tree truncation with AI feedback
ai.summary: File tree truncation logic in `truncate-file-tree.ts` now uses a four-level fallback strategy: full tree, removal of unimportant files, removal of token counts, and finally depth-based pruning. The `getProjectFileTreePrompt` function in `system-prompt.ts` injects specific notes into the context to inform the AI which truncation level was applied. This replaces the previous binary fallback that often discarded too much structure. Internal docs in `knowledge.md` updated to reflect the new hierarchy.

eli5.text: When the AI helper looks at your project's file structure, it no longer has to choose between showing everything or cutting out large chunks at random. Now it tries four gentler steps in order: first dropping token counts, then hiding build artifacts and cache files, then pruning the deepest directories only if needed. The helper is also told in plain words which step it ended up using, so it understands what it's missing and can work around it instead of guessing. The change went live today as part of the internal backend tooling that powers the assistant's project awareness.

ai.title: Fix terminal timeout for silent commands
ai.summary: Silent commands no longer hang the terminal. `runCommandPty` in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` now wraps commands with shell conditionals to detect completion. `npm-app/knowledge.md` documents the new ANSI color and exit code handling.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs commands in the terminal, some commands don't print anything while they work, and the terminal would just sit there forever waiting. Now the code wraps those commands so that when they finish, the terminal automatically prints whether it succeeded or failed, and it stops hanging. You'd notice the difference if you ran the assistant and it tried to run a silent command, it would actually complete and tell you the result instead of freezing.

ai.title: Version 1.0.150
ai.summary: Bump npm-app package.json version from 1.0.149 to 1.0.150. Internal release preparation.

eli5.text: The app you open now shows version 1.0.150 instead of the old number, and that is the only visible change in this particular update. Behind that version label sits a week of fixes and small upgrades: tab completion in the command line is now case-insensitive, the assistant no longer gets stuck when a silent command finishes without typing anything, and the system now picks up to date web knowledge instead of stale docs left over from older modes. The version bump itself is live today.
